h1: What are the zoning and permit rules for a detached garage in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Detached Garage Rules: Permits, Setbacks and Zoning
description: Review Newton's accessory-building location rules and the building permit process before planning a detached garage.
short_answer: A new detached garage is a building project that should be reviewed by Newton ISD and checked against the property's zoning district. Newton's accessory-building rules generally require at least 5 feet from side and rear lot lines and at least 5 feet from the principal building. Height, footprint, lot coverage, and any required zoning relief must be checked separately.

facts.text: The state building code generally requires a permit before constructing a regulated building or structure.
Newton's accessory-building ordinance generally requires 5 feet from side and rear lot lines and 5 feet from the principal building on the same lot.

qa.q: Can I place a detached garage 5 feet from every lot line?
qa.a: No. The 5-foot rule applies to side and rear lot lines. The front setback follows the principal building's required front setback, and other zoning standards may apply.

items: The property's zoning district and whether the lot is conforming
The allowed garage height, story count, and footprint
Lot coverage, open space, and driveway access
Whether a special permit or other zoning relief is required
Any historic, tree, stormwater, wetlands, or floodplain review
